ConceptInfo.Civilopedia: [H1]Alien Civilizations:[\H1] The alien races (natives) are now enabled as playable civilizations. They begin with several existing settlements via Advanced Start and maintain an advantage in harvesting native resources, but are much slower than humans at developing advanced infrastructure and manufactured goods.[NEWLINE][H1]Alien Economy:[\H1][NEWLINE]The alien races have a significant advantage in starting with settlements already populated and established. However, living in a state of pastoral anarchy, each alien settlment must construct a [LINK=BUILDING_ZIGGURAT]Ziggurat[\LINK] in each settlement to enable further organized development, effectively giving Human players a 50-turn head start. The Ziggurat also functions as a basic market building to represent the aliens' internal economy; enabling each settlement to automatically sell excess resources at a small fraction of the price on Earth. This ratio can be increased by constructing buildings such as the [LINK=BUILDING_LANDINGPAD]Landing Pad[\LINK] to enable offworld trade with independent smugglers; however, the true profits will come from eventually gaining direct access to the distant markets of Earth.[NEWLINE][H1]Aliens and Earth:[\H1][NEWLINE]After gathering sufficient industrial goods and building an Alien Shipyard, aliens may construct a variety of space vessels such as the [LINK=UNIT_SAUCER]Saucer[\LINK] and [LINK=UNIT_UFO]UFO[\LINK], and can eventually discover and enter the wormhole to Earth. (Note that Alien Saucers use a different propulsion mechanism than the Earthling vessels, which are restricted to Deep Space and Low Orbit tiles. By right-clicking over a planet's interior, a Saucer can fly through the entirety of its atmosphere, reaching colonies not directly accessible to Earthling ships.) Due to the monopolistic practices of the Earth superpowers, aliens can only conduct covert trade with disenfranchised Third World nations, and the market prices they receive will be much less favorable than human colonies. Nevertheless, smuggling goods to the black markets of Earth can prove a vital lifeline for alien civilizations. [NEWLINE][H1]Aliens and Human Colonists:[\H1][NEWLINE]The political situation in some Earthling nations has become so intolerable that some aliens are able to abduct a steady trickle of human colonists to their worlds by building an [LINK=BUILDING_HABITAT]Earthling Habitat[\LINK] in their cities to generate Propaganda. Although aliens again have a severe disadvantage in attracting emigrants compared to the human colonies, the manufacturing skills of even unspecialized human colonists make them greatly prized among the species of the New Worlds. Abducting human colonists by force is another alternative to gain access to their skills - on conquering a human colony, aliens can obtain enough Earthling tissue to create a [LINK=UNIT_HUMANHYBRID]Human Hybrid[\LINK] who will also work in manufacturing facilities much more efficiently than the aliens themselves.[NEWLINE][H1]Aliens and Liberty:[\H1][NEWLINE]Previously accustomed to unquestioning obedience to the tyranny of the long-absent Progenitors, the arrival of the Earthlings stimulated many alien elders to return to the ways of their ancient mystery traditions in search of enlightenment and power. Long dismissed as the rantings of conspiracy theorists, secret societies such as the [LINK=BUILDING_ILLUMINATED_CIRCLE]Illuminati[\LINK] have covertly permeated alien and human societies for centuries, and have many secret adherents among certain select members of the Earth elite. Through deep connections to this far-reaching conspiracy, the alien elders of an Illuminati Lodge could begin to challenge the dominance of the Progenitors among their race, and even attract highly-placed human Directors to conspire with their agenda.[NEWLINE][H1]Alien Specialists:[\H1][NEWLINE]With sufficient resources, aliens may eventually train elite members of their species that are much more versatile than the narrowly-focused human specialists, though slightly less effective in each individual field. The [LINK=UNIT_CYBORG]Industrious Cyborg[\LINK] produces Hammers, Tools, and Weapons nearly as efficiently as human specialists, the [LINK=UNIT_POLYMATH]Brilliant Polymath[\LINK] can approach the abilities of a human Physicist, Biochemist, Drug Runner, and Theorist all in one, and the [LINK=UNIT_ELDER]Venerable Elder[\LINK] can generate Liberty by working in an Elder Council or Menhir, as well as planning the abduction of human servants from Earth through work in an Earthling Habitat or Abduction Site.[NEWLINE][H1]Alien Improvements:[\H1][NEWLINE]A number of secret alien sites are scattered across the New Worlds, though many are quickly ransacked for treasure by the Earthling imperialists. If these sites can be captured and protected, a Venerable Elder working as a Ritualist on a tile containing a sacred [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_MENHIR]Menhir[\LINK] can be a powerful force for Liberty, or an Elder working at an [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_ALTAR]Abduction Site[\LINK] can engineer the abduction of human servitors from Earth. With enough Biotech, aliens can train a [LINK=UNIT_CULTIVATOR]Cultivator[\LINK] capable of building Alien Garden and Alien Burrow improvements, that given time will develop into rich Plantation and Cavern complexes that create significant wealth.

[H1]Technologies:[\H1]There is a new "Research" icon (light bulb) at the top of the screen. Click on this to bring up the Research Advisor. The Research Screen is similar to the Civ4 Tech screen. You can scroll up or down to view all the techs. Mouse over all the techs to see what they have to offer. Techs currently available for research will say "Click to Research". The current Tech you are researching will be highlighted, and the number of turns to complete will appear at the bottom of the screen. Completed research is labeled with a darkened background.[NEWLINE]To start learning new techs, assign one of your colonists to the Research Lab in your city screen (or one of its upgrades, the Research Institute or Research Complex, or the Shamanic Lodge if playing an alien race). Production of each unit of Research (bulbs) consumes one unit of one or more different resources, depending on the tech. Some of the more advanced technologies can also require that a specific colonist type be assisting on the project.[NEWLINE]In the City Screen, you can mouse over the "Research" lightbulb icon to see the current project, resources consumed, current progress, and turns to complete. You can also change projects here by clicking on the Research icon.[NEWLINE][H1]New Unit - Visionary Researcher:[\H1]This scientific mastermind doubles the output of Research. Each unit of research produced in your colonies adds to a meter that stimulates emigration of a Visionary Researcher from Earth.[NEWLINE][H1]Tech Trading and Research Pacts:[\H1]The AI players will also start to do their own Research Projects. You can trade techs and form Research Pacts to make more rapid progress, or hoard your technology for a strategic edge. Other players will accassionaly ask to make tech trades with you. Alien races start with foreknowledge of several special Xenoscience techs, but find mastery of advanced Human technology difficult.[NEWLINE][H1]Research Strategy:[\H1]You will begin with access to a limited number of colonists, professions, and resource types and will need to unlock access to these gradually with the progress of research. Researching appropriate technologies can also unlock the benefits of bonus resources distributed across the map, such as the Iridescent Pyramids and Obsidian Faces. Development can be much more challenging than in the unmodified game, but the rewards of mastering advanced technology can be great. At higher difficulty levels, strategic use of technological progress may be essential to win Independence.

[H1]Sites and Expeditions:[\H1]A variety of rare and mysterious sites such as [LINK=BONUS_TEMPLE]Ruined Temples[\LINK] and [LINK=BONUS_PYRAMID]Iridescent Pyramids[\LINK]can be found dotted throughout the ruins and forests of the New Worlds. See Bonus Resources in the Civilopedia for a complete list and descriptions. After obtaining control of one of these sites, an Intrepid Explorer or Intrepid Archaeologist assigned to the Laborer profession can be moved to the tile and ordered to begin an Expedition there. This consumes the unit, but can greatly increase the amount and variety of resources that can harvested from the site, particularly after discovering later technologies that boost the yield of Expeditions.

[H1]Alien Flora and Fauna:[\H1]The New Worlds are home to a wide variety of unusual plant and animal species, many of which require the discovery of advanced technology to benefit fully from their potential uses. Several species are endemic to only one of the New Worlds planets, which may require colonial outposts on several planets if you want to benefit from each of their unique advantages. After discovering Interplanetary Ecology, your Laborers can build a Pasture on tiles with native animals to gain extra yields from their domestication.

[H1]Alien UFOs:[\H1]Even while presenting a facade of benign altruism to the Earthling interlopers, hidden saucers under the control of less sympathetic Alien Elders rained devastation upon unwary human colonists who were rash enough to venture into the New Worlds unprotected. The quick human Corvettes rapidly grew adept in Evasive Maneuvers, hiding in Low Orbit and strategic Asteroid Belts where they could often outmaneuver more powerful craft, and building colonial networks of Spaceports and Drydocks for damaged vessels to find refuge and repair.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE]Alien Saucers use a mysterious propulsion mechanism than the massive Resonance Drives used by Earthling vessels, which enable humans to traverse the wormhole more rapidly but restrict them to Deep Space and Low Orbit tiles. By right-clicking over a planet's interior, an Alien Saucer can fly through the entirety of its atmosphere, reaching sites and colonies not directly accessible to Earthling ships. This leaves unwary Earthlings vulnerable to abduction by their alien neighbors. After discovering Xenolinguistics, units accompanied by an Alien Guide may receive forewarning of UFO attacks.

[H1]The Progenitors:[\H1]The New Worlds are littered with the ruins of an ancient civilization called the Progenitors, who appear to have been masters of powerful and nearly incomprehensible technology. Many of the richest sites lie frozen under sheets of ice in uninhabitable polar regions; these arctic climates have preserved many remnants remarkably well; it is also believed that the Progenitors favored freezing temperatures as their nervous system has certain semiconductor properties. Although the Progenitors have long been absent, the native alien races of the New Worlds remain under their tyranny, forced to pay over ever-escalating tithes. But perhaps the unexpected arrival of the Earthlings and their strange sciences will provide a catalyst for the aliens to shake off their masters' chains?[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][H1]Progenitor Artifacts[\H1]Though their inner workings remain far beyond current human understanding, Progenitor Artifacts are in utmost demand among the scientists and governments of Earth. After discovering the necessary technologies, colonists working as a Theorist in buildings such as the Progenitor Research Lab can process raw Artifacts into even more valuable Progenitor Tech.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][H1]Progenitor Ruins[\H1]Looming among the ruins are several rings of titanic monoliths indicating the site of an abandoned Progenitor Metropolis, These sites are particularly rich in any manner of goods and technologies; but are often guarded by lethal Progenitor Killbots or entombed in an Ancient Mounds that only a Hardy Laborer can excavate. After successfully capturing a Metropolis and discovering the technology necessary for advanced professions such as the Quantum Physicist and Symbologist, your colonists can access unusually powerful buildings such as a Progenitor Reactor or Ancient Databank, directly producing advanced goods such as Fusion Cores and Research without the need for time-consuming manufacture and processing from raw goods inside colonial buildings.

[H1]Moons and Lunar Colonies:[\H1]Some planets among the New Worlds are orbited by a variety of small moons, each having a unique ecosystem and composition. Thought to be the remnants of Progenitor experiments in terraforming, these planetoids' unusually dense cores enables them to maintain some semblance of an atmosphere. On moons in orbit close to an existing planetary settlement, a Colony Ship can found a Lunar Outpost, which over time can develop into a prosperous Lunar Settlement and later a Lunar Colony as the tile is worked by its parent city. Although colonizing the tiny planetoids orbiting the New Worlds required a huge upfront investment in time and supplies, a mature Lunar Colony could eventually yield rich resources for export to its parent settlement on the planet below.[NEWLINE][NEWLINE][H1]Atmospheres and Terraforming:[\H1]With the appropriate technology, the delicate instruments carried by a Science Vessel can permit successful terraforming of the noxious atmospheres common to the New Worlds' resource-rich moons, further enhancing the yield of a resident Lunar Colony.

[H1]Asteroid Mining and Anomalies[\H1]The robotic armatures of a Mining Vessel can extract valuable resources from the various asteroid belts and space debris scattered across the deep space surrounding the New Worlds. Additionally, the advanced but delicate research instruments carried by a Science Vessel can harvest valuable research data and scientific goods from the strange deep space anomalies prevalent in close proximity to the wormhole.
